doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Dream playing wish: Milt Jackson
summary: He would love to play with Milt Jackson and prefers bebop.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: If you could write your own ticket for the next three or four years — play with anybody, go anywhere, do anything, your dream requisition — what would be on it?

Well like I told Mike LeDonne, I’d like to play with Milt Jackson. There’s so few guys around, well you know like I said I liked Sonny Rollins the way he used to play back 30 years ago. And I still like him, he’s a wonderful guy, it’s just that he’s so far out. But I mean anyhow, I would like to play with, you know like I say I’m old enough that I started with the old even Dixieland you know I played with a lot of Dixieland bands too. And I don’t put any of that down. But I just happened to, my favorite is sort of bebop kind of music, you know and I’d love to be able to play with somebody like Milt Jackson because he’s one of the few outstanding guys I can think of that can lead a quartet. So that would be my ultimate I guess. Yeah.
